sentences.text:
Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner no.1 and 2 are the children of the deceased Sri.Yohannan Lalu and petitioner no.3.

That on 24.02.2025 at about 02.50 pm, Yohannan Lal S/o Joseph was riding the motorcycle beg. Reg. No,KA-21-EE-5902, in Hosakote Devanahalli Road, near IB circle, wherein the driver of Eicher Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-07-B-8374, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident, in the accident Yohannan Lal sustained grievous injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries on the spot.

His body was shifted to MVJ Hospital,
wherein PM was conducted.
The petitioners have performed funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioners alleged that deceased was 57 yeas of age as on the date of accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was working as a Farmer and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month and he was the only earning member for their family.

They alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.54/2025.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.1 is the insurer, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondent no.2 has not chosen to appear before this tribunal and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire version of the petition in toto.
Respondent No.1 has specifically denied the age, income of the deceased.
Respondent No.1 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the deceased and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW-1, produced and marked 13 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 13 and he is fully cross examined.
Respondent No.1 has not chosen to lead the evidence after obtaining sufficient opportunity from this tribunal.
Hence respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil.
7. I have heard the arguments form the counsels appearing for both the sides.
I have perused the entire records.

8. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES

sentences.text: 1.Whether the petitioners prove that on 24.02.2025 at about 02.50 pm, Yohannan Lal S/o Joseph was riding the motorcycle beg. Reg. No,KA-21-EE-5902, in Hosakote Devanahalli Road, near IB circle, wherein the driver of Eicher Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-07-B-8374, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident, in the accident Yohannan Lal sustained grievous injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries as alleged in the petition.?
2. Whether respondent no.1 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions as contended in the written statement.?

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?

9. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 ISSUE No.1: In the Affirmative,
 ISSUE No.2: In the Negative  ISSUE No.3: In partly affirmative,
 ISSUE No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  10. ISSUES No.1 to 3 :- I have taken both the issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.1 and Son of the deceased Yohannan Lalu, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
11. According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In order to prove the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners have tendered the FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch, IMV report,
Inquest, PM report, final report, which are at Ex.P1 to 9.
12.

On perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that Yohaman Lalu died in the motor vehicle road accident caused by the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle that is Suheeb Ulla Khan S/o Mustaq ualla Khan.
It is evident that Suheeb Ulla Khan S/o Mustaq ualla Khan, was the driver of the offending vehicle,

Ex.P11 is the reply notice given by the respondent No.2 to the notice issued U/s 133 of IMV Act, wherein he admit that his driver was having valid DL and the policy of the vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident.
In the cross examination of PW-1, nothing worth is elicited to disbelieve the petitioner version.

Respondent No.1 has failed to establish its contention that respondent No.2 has violated the policy condition and accident Jobin Laal vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62210520/
3 occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.

sentences.text: Further more final report which is at Ex.P.9 is filed after thorough investigation and it is not disputed by the respondents as such it has attained the finality.

Respondent no.1 has not chosen to lead evidence it shows that respondent No.1 has admitted the negligent act of his driver and respondent No.1 have admitted their liability to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

13. Petitioners have not tendered the evidence to substantiate the nature of work and the income of the deceased accordingly the notional income of Rs.17,000/- has to be considered as the income of the deceased as the accident occurred in the year 2025.
14. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the deceased is 11.08.1967.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 57 years and multiplier 9 is applicable.
15. Deceased was self employee, married and he was above 50 years, accordingly 10% should be added towards his monthly income for future prospectus.
Deceased left behind 2 dependents accordingly 1/3 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

16. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs. 17,000/-
Add: 10% of income future prospectus Rs. 1,700/-
 Monthly income Rs. 18,700/-
2 Less; 1/3 for personal expenses Rs. 6,233/-
4 Monthly income Rs. 12,467/-
 Rs.12,467 (income)X 12 (month) X 9 Rs.13,46,436/-
 (Multiplier )
 Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.13,46,436/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.
17. Loss of estate;

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.
18 . Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.
19. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept Jobin Laal vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62210520/
4 of consortium is categorically discussed.

sentences.text:
In the present case petitioners are the Children of late Yohannan Lalu and they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/-
each.
Accordingly they are entitled for Rs.80,000/- as compensation under this head.
Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.
20. In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl Compensation
under the Head
Amount No. 1 Loss of dependency Rs.13,46,436/-

2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3
Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 80,000/-
In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.14,56,436/-.
21. Rate of Interest: The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s
Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
22. Liability:

Admittedly the validity of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is not disputed nor denied by the respondent No.1 and they have not probabilise their contention, accordingly Respondent No.1 being the insurer has to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioners.
Accordingly respondent no.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.

Accordingly I am answering Issue no.1 in the affirmative, Issue No.2 in the negative and Issue no.3 in partly affirmative,
23. Issue No.3;

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.14,56,436/- with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for 50%, each in the total compensation amount with interest.
